new.why: Databricks published an October 23 benchmark comparing declarative and procedural Spark targets across 528 agent-built pipelines.
new.summary: Declarative agent-authored pipelines describe desired datasets while the execution engine validates structure, orders dependencies and handles repeated operational boilerplate.
new.why_now: Databricks reported lower compute time and less code on October 23, creating a measurable baseline that still needs independent reproduction.
new.practical_value: Data teams can compare one bounded pipeline across both interfaces using dry-run failures, compute time, code volume and reviewer correction effort.

evidence.title: Built for Agents: The Case for Spark Declarative Pipelines

novelty.reason: The benchmark directly compares two pipeline interfaces under the same agent-building workload rather than reporting generic coding-agent productivity.

evidence.reason: Databricks documents 528 tasks, structural checks, compute-time and code-volume results, though all measurements remain publisher-run.

independence.reason: No independent operator reproduced the benchmark on another engine, agent or production data workload during this review.

momentum.reason: One dated benchmark provides no second comparable observation under a stable declarative-pipeline adoption or performance metric.

relevance.reason: Data engineering teams can reproduce a bounded comparison using dry-run failures, compute consumption, code volume and reviewer effort.

durability.reason: Declarative validation and engine-managed dependencies remain useful design principles even as agents, models and execution systems change.

carried_forward.why: OpenAI’s October 23 incident account supplies a dated pause, adversarial test and restart sequence for a frontier-model training environment.

carried_forward.practical_value: Security teams can test whether network isolation, monitoring, escalation and restart criteria hold under realistic agent-driven attack scenarios.
